''See also: [[Soulbound Timeline]]''

== Overview ==
{{spoiler|book=ee-shadow-03-of-killers-and-kings|Soulbound are individuals who have formed a profound, symbiotic connection with an [[Awakened object]] known as a [[Vessel]]. This bond is achieved through a process involving [[Intent]] and [[Awakening]], which allows the individual to draw upon the supernatural abilities of an Elder or a [[Kameira]]. While most Soulbound possess unique gifts—such as the ability to manipulate fire, enhance physical strength, or control sand—the specific nature of their power is determined by the characteristics of their [[Vessel]]. Some Soulbound may even experience their [[Vessels]] as conscious entities, hearing voices or feeling desires that are inextricably linked to their own. In [[The Empire|the Empire]], Soulbound are highly significant and officially registered figures. They serve in various vital roles, including as elite warriors, specialized craftsmen, communicators over long distances, and even navigators bound to ships. Some of the most legendary figures in history were Soulbound who performed miraculous feats on the battlefield. However, this power comes with vulnerabilities; a Soulbound's strength is tied to their [[Vessel]], and identifying or seizing the object is a primary tactic for neutralizing them. The initial period following the bonding process can be particularly unstable, as the individual must learn to manage the intense urges and complexities of their new connection. While Soulbound are immensely powerful, they are distinct from [[Champions]], who are superhuman warriors specifically trained from birth for combat.}}

== Of Sea and Shadow ==
{{spoiler|book=ee-sea-01-of-sea-and-shadow|Soulbound is a status held by humans who undergo the process of [[Awakening]] to borrow powers from [[Kameira]] or the [[Elders]]. While it is believed that all [[Greenwardens]] are Soulbound, only a small number of these individuals exist on the continent. These warriors serve as The Empire{{!}}the Empire's greatest fighters, possessing useful abilities and even the capacity to wield power freely. Although it can take years for one to bond a [[Vessel]], every Soulbound maintains a connection to her [[Vessel]] and can fight her way to freedom if brought to it. Among the crew, two such individuals are known, including [[Naberius Clayborn]], and one has even breached [[Bastion's Veil|Bastion’s Veil]]. While a Soulbound is distinct from a [[Champion]], they would still struggle against the focused power of Urzaia Woodsman{{!}}Urzaia's opponent.}}

== Of Shadow and Sea ==
{{spoiler|book=ee-shadow-01-of-shadow-and-sea|A Soulbound is a person who has bonded with an object of power, known as a [[Vessel]], from which they draw their strength. These entities may receive specific powers through this connection, and their relationship to [[Intent]] remains a significant subject of concern. While certain types exist, such as the Soulbound [[Silent One]], all [[Gardeners]] avoid fighting them at any cost. This classification includes Navigators, who are each bound to their respective ships, and it also encompasses individuals like [[Bastion]]. If [[Naberius Clayborn]] were to take the Heart as his [[Vessel]], he would undergo this transformation.}}

== Of Dawn and Darkness ==
{{spoiler|book=ee-sea-02-of-dawn-and-darkness|A Soulbound is a legendary fighter and a type of person [[Jyrine Tessella Marten|Jyrine]] has long dreamed of meeting. These individuals are born through the phenomena of [[Reading]] and [[Intent]], possessing something to bind and powers that remain not fully understood. Because conventional arms are ineffective against them, Soulbound entities and combat-capable modifications have been mobilized, appearing as beacons within [[The Testament]]'s awareness. [[Shera]] is identified as a Soulbound who can call for her [[Vessel]], leading [[Jerri]] to question what makes her more dangerous than others of her kind. This classification is a subject of inquiry for [[Calder]] and [[Duster]], especially following the involvement of a Soulbound in the attack on [[Mekendi Maxeus]].}}

== Of Darkness and Dawn ==
{{spoiler|book=ee-shadow-02-of-darkness-and-dawn|As one of the world's first Soulbound, [[Alagaeus]] belongs to a vital group within [[The Empire|the Empire]] that possesses a link to specific [[Vessels]]. These individuals, such as [[Jyrine Tessella Marten|Jyrine]], derive their power from either an Elder or a [[Kameira]] and must navigate a critical first few months while harnessing that [[Elder power]]. While some Soulbound like [[Shera]] may exist without their [[Vessel]], others can draw strength by inhaling through a blade. Despite being capable of being subdued by the [[Imperial Guard]], Soulbound remain difficult for mortal judges to oversee with precision or impartiality.}}

== Of Kings and Killers ==
{{spoiler|book=ee-sea-03-of-kings-and-killers|Soulbound is a form of magic that can be an achievement, a state of being, or a power possessed by [[Luminian Order]] [[Pilgrims]]. This ability allows individuals to perform immense feats, such as reshaping the [[Spear of Tharlos]] or raising an entire island from the sea. While [[Alchemists|alchemists]] utilize leashed Soulbound, those with this power must leave their [[Vessels]] in secure storage before meetings, a process that feels like a loss of physical sensation. The nature of this power is highly regulated, as [[Champions]] must meet specific requirements and the [[Luminian Order]]'s support has left very few Soulbound capable of healing. In combat, a Soulbound like [[Varia Selethir]] is formidable, and if [[Jerri]] is unarmed, [[Calder]] finds himself unable to defend against one. Furthermore, certain Soulbound have been hired for specialized tasks, such as projecting illusions to lure [[Bliss of the Blackwatch|Bliss]] away from the Capital.}}

== Of Killers and Kings ==
{{spoiler|book=ee-shadow-03-of-killers-and-kings|Soulbound are volatile individuals who can be newly acquired through a process that allows people to emerge successfully transformed. These entities possess powers of communication and, in some historical instances, the ability to alter their voice and appearance. To master their nature, a Soulbound must plumb the depths of their [[Vessel]] and uncover various layers of [[Intent]]. While they have unleashed their powers within the streets of the [[Imperial]] Palace, truly powerful Soulbound are capable of destroying the [[Shades of Urg’naut]]. Due to their strength, [[Shera]] maintains a small army of these individuals and has expressed a need for more Soulbound who are capable in combat.}}

<li>{{spoiler|book=ee-shadow-03-of-killers-and-kings|Powerful [[Soulbound]] can destroy the [[Shades of Urg’naut]].<ref name="ee-shadow-03-of-killers-and-kings-c20">''Of Killers and Kings'', chapter 20</ref>}}</li>

<li>{{spoiler|book=ee-shadow-03-of-killers-and-kings|[[Soulbound]] have powers of communication.<ref name="ee-shadow-03-of-killers-and-kings-c22" />}}</li>
<li>{{spoiler|book=ee-shadow-03-of-killers-and-kings|[[Soulbound]] are entities that can be newly acquired.<ref name="ee-shadow-03-of-killers-and-kings-c22" />}}</li>
<li>{{spoiler|book=ee-shadow-03-of-killers-and-kings|[[Soulbinding]] is a process where people can come out successfully [[Soulbound]].<ref name="ee-shadow-03-of-killers-and-kings-c22" />}}</li>
<li>{{spoiler|book=ee-shadow-03-of-killers-and-kings|[[Shera]] has a small army of [[Soulbound]].<ref name="ee-shadow-03-of-killers-and-kings-c25">''Of Killers and Kings'', chapter 25</ref>}}</li>
<li>{{spoiler|book=ee-shadow-03-of-killers-and-kings|[[Awakened weapons]] assault the [[Dead Mother]] like an army of [[Soulbound]].<ref name="ee-shadow-03-of-killers-and-kings-c26">''Of Killers and Kings'', chapter 26</ref>}}</li>
</ul></div>
